_meta.description: Permanent failure database: one structured entry per killed strategy/cell. Companion to RESEARCH_LOG prose; the log holds the full record, this holds the queryable skeleton. Lesson tags are a controlled vocabulary: spread-eaten | windfall-year | trend-bleed | regime-non-transfer | no-edge | min-N-starvation | stale-mechanism | measurement-uninformative.
_meta.convention: numeric_reason quotes the kill-deciding numbers; log_ref is the adjudicating commit where known

entries.hypothesis: RSI crossover mean-reversion entries carry a candle-scale edge

entries.hypothesis: The NY-close/Sydney-open liquidity trough (17:00-19:00 ET) produces a structural, mechanism-based price dislocation distinct from price-action mean reversion
entries.kill_stage: PARTIAL REJECT at overshoot-vs-real-cost gate -- pre-declared kill condition (cost dominates on ALL three pairs, or events too rare) NOT met; rejected on portfolio-concentration grounds by operator decision, not mechanism failure
entries.numeric_reason: mechanism CONFIRMED cross-pair (window tick volume 0.30-0.64x flanking hours, per-print volatility amplified 1.6-2.3x, DST spot-checked clean on 4 dates); tradeable residual after REAL spread (OANDA MBA candles): rev/cost across N=2/3/4 thresholds AUD_USD 0.97-1.04 and NZD_USD 0.89-0.97 (cost-dominated), USD_JPY 1.11-1.55 but UPPER-BOUND (reversion measured from unreachable window extreme; only 56% of events clear cost, mean carried by fat right tail); quoted spread spikes 1.3-1.6p -> 8-10p at the 17:00 rollover
entries.lesson: Execution cost is worst exactly when the liquidity edge occurs -- the rollover spread spike consumes the overshoot on 2 of 3 pairs and thins the third. Same failure signature as the pair-expansion (trend-origin transfer) line: mechanism generalizes cross-pair, tradeable payoff is USD_JPY-only, which duplicates existing ~85% fleet USD_JPY concentration instead of adding an uncorrelated bet. NOT a flat kill -- reopen bar: genuinely cross-pair tradeable residual after real spread cost, with reversion measured from an EXECUTABLE entry (not the window extreme), clearing cost on AUD_USD or NZD_USD, not just USD_JPY. Artifacts: liquidity_trough_check.py/.png, trough_overshoot_check.py/.png

entries.hypothesis: The measured ~1R median MFE giveback (mechanism: fixed 2.5R target overshoots regime-dependent leg length; 24-26% of +1R-touchers round-trip to SL) can be converted to realized R by (1) breakeven-after-+1R, (2) 50% partial at +1.25R, or (3) 0.75R ratchet trail after +1R
entries.kill_stage: Gate 1 (held-out 2024-2026 window, 4,987 trades) with Gate-2 exit costs (0.03R per triggered exit) included; simulated on conservative low-based mark paths
entries.numeric_reason: Held-out mean-R deltas vs fire-and-forget baseline -- rule 2 (partial): intraday -0.088R, scalp30 -0.116R, pullback30 -0.056R (decisive fail); rule 3 (trail): -0.020R/-0.035R/+0.032R; rule 1 (BE+): -0.016R/-0.026R/+0.032R. Rule 1's Donchian deltas are within the low-based-marks bias band (verdict: no demonstrated improvement, not proven harm); pullback30's positive delta sign-flips vs the design window (unstable)
entries.lesson: The giveback is real (median 1R) but it is the PRICE of the 2.5R tail that funds the whole expectancy: every interference with the path forfeits tail winners at roughly the rate it saves round-trippers. Whipsaw tax >= giveback savings on M30/H1 trend entries. The coherent Gate-0 mechanism (regime-dependent leg exhaustion) survives -- what failed is converting it into a path-based exit at these timeframes. Reopen bar: an exit rule keyed to a REGIME measurement (not path levels), or bar-level high/low re-simulation showing rule 1's true delta clears +0.02R held-out on the Donchians.
entries.log_ref: not committed (operator constraint: no git this study); analysis in-session

entries.hypothesis: The exit-rule study's two reopen paths: (1) bar-level high/low re-simulation shows rule 1's true delta clears +0.02R held-out; (2) regime-gating rule 1 (active only when daily ER(20) < 0.20 at entry, standing convention) converts the coherent regime mechanism into a net-positive exit
entries.class: exit-rule overlay (fleet trend strategies), reopen of exit_rules_giveback_study_2026_07
entries.kill_stage: bar-accurate replay on true OANDA M30 highs/lows (347k bars, 5 pairs), 0.03R exit costs, design/held-out split
entries.numeric_reason: Held-out 2024-2026 mean-R deltas vs baseline: rule1-always intraday -0.049R / scalp30 -0.088R / pullback30 -0.046R (bar-level triggers via true highs INCREASE whipsaw vs the low-based marks estimate -- the bias correction went AGAINST the rule); rule1-regime-gated -0.027R / -0.048R / +0.002R -- the gate roughly halves the damage everywhere (direction confirms the regime mechanism) but crosses zero nowhere
entries.lesson: Both reopen paths dead. Bar-level truth is harsher than the conservative marks bound: true-high triggers fire more often, so more eventual winners get breakeven'd out. The regime gate is directionally right (ranging-regime trades are where BE protection hurts least) yet still net-negative held-out -- the whipsaw tax exceeds giveback savings even in the regime the mechanism targets. Fire-and-forget is confirmed near-optimal for these designs at bar-level fidelity. Reopen bar: an exit design that avoids path-level stops entirely (e.g., regime-triggered position REDUCTION at entry time, not in-flight), registered on its own merits.
entries.log_ref: not committed (operator constraint); in-session analysis, exit_rule_barlevel.log

entries.hypothesis: 0.5x risk on entries taken at daily ER(20) < 0.20 (own instrument, completed days only) improves the trial book's risk-adjusted return -- the sizing form of the exit study's surviving leg-exhaustion mechanism

entries.kill_stage: Gates M and H, both decisive (registration ab18f69 committed before results)
entries.numeric_reason: Gate M: book design-window gap trending-ranging = -0.090R (needed >= +0.05R) -- ranging entries EARNED MORE on the trial book, opposite ordering; fleet corroboration ordering held (+0.040R) but the deploy evidence contradicts it. Gate H: held-out ret/maxDD 11.91 -> 12.05 (+1.2%, needed >= +10%). Per-slot signs flip across windows everywhere (xau design ranging+0.28/trending-0.13 vs heldout ranging+0.05/trending+0.50)
entries.lesson: The regime-dependent leg-exhaustion mechanism was measured on fleet FX M30 trend entries; it does not transfer to this book as a sizing overlay -- the gold/index pullback and ORB slots show no stable ranging-regime penalty, and per-slot regime orderings flip sign between design and held-out windows. A regime dial that flips sign across windows cannot size anything. Exit-study reopen bar now fully closed: path-based exits dead (entries 42-43), entry-time sizing dead (this entry). Fire-and-forget at fixed fractional risk stands as the book's complete trade-management answer.

Confirms the original triage's own caveat (extreme-entry generosity was the number's weakest link) and generalizes: a liquidity-calendar edge whose signal and decay both occur within the illiquid window cannot be harvested from outside it. Reopen bar UNMET; the line stays closed with the executable-entry question now answered, not assumed.

entries.hypothesis: Cross-sectional relative strength among SPX/NQ/YM (rank by 20d return; long top / short bottom intraday 09:30-16:00 ET, 1xATR stop) carries an edge as a day-neutral pair
entries.numeric_reason: combined n=342, -$1.54/trade; short leg -$5.30/trade (n=171) overwhelms the long leg's +$2.21 (n=171)
entries.lesson: Relative 20d strength does not predict intraday relative performance among the US index family -- the family is too cointegrated at day horizon for yesterday's ranking to matter, and shorting the 'weakest' index intraday fights the shared upward drift both legs were supposed to hedge out. Honesty note (adjacent, NOT pursued): the long leg alone was positive in the quick-check year; a 'long-strongest-only' design would be a post-hoc amputation of a failed construction and is not a registered candidate.

entries.lesson: The rung-transfer warning fires again, with a twist: the M15 rung PASSED its quick-check year because the quick-check year WAS the windfall. Full-window adjudication caught it. The validated M30 SPX pullback's edge does not live at M15 -- deteriorating three years straight there while the M30 rung stays deployed. Gold's M15 rungs passing while SPX's fails also breaks any 'M15 works' generalization: rung viability is instrument-specific, same as mechanism transfer.

entries.hypothesis: The validated ORB session-momentum mechanism transfers from the US 09:30 open to gold's London 08:00 open (identical close-variant mechanics, UK statutory DST clock)
entries.kill_stage: Line-B kill-test stretches, both negative (registration c1dd8c2; UK clock 8/8 boundary dates hand-verified pre-run)
entries.numeric_reason: A2023: n=231, net -$1,066.56, WR 39.8%; B24H2: n=342, net -$492.83, WR 40.4% (criteria: both stretches net-positive AND n>=30)
entries.lesson: Session-momentum is not a property of 'session opens' generally -- it is a property of the US equity-market open specifically. The London open produces ranges that break and revert at ~40% WR against a 2x-height target on the very instrument (gold) where the US-open version passed. Family extensions across SESSIONS now have the same instrument-specific warning as extensions across instruments (orb_nq redundancy, YM fragility).
